3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I was in my office reading reports from the ministries about the current situation of the protests.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: My next scheduled meeting was with Nia and Lileas, to discuss the law enforcement budget. I heard some knocks on the door.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Nia entered and took a seat in front of my desk. Lileas was absent.

7.speaker: Nia Morgna
7.text: “Lileas will be late. Apparently there was an urgent matter at the Ministry of the Interior she had to attend to. Shouldn't take long.”

10.speaker: Nia Morgna
10.text: “While we wait, why don't we have a little chat?”

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “That's a couple of minutes less of Lileas. Great.”

15.speaker: Nia Morgna
15.text: “She said something about supply distribution for the police forces. Nothing major.”

16.speaker: Nia Morgna
16.text: “You wouldn't find many who think otherwise.”

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: I returned to my reports and Nia smoothed back an errant strand of her hair. There was an awkward silence.

19.speaker: Nia Morgna
19.text: “This might come off as a little strange, but I am proud of you.”

20.speaker: Nia Morgna
20.text: “Despite everything, you are actually trying to reform the country.”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “It's *we* Nia, not *me*. I couldn't do any of this by myself. So no, I am proud of you.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “Flattery won't work on me. What do you want?”

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “This is just the beginning. There is so much more to do.”

25.speaker: Nia Morgna
25.text: “You certainly have a way with words, don't you?”

26.speaker: Nia Morgna
26.text: “Yes. Although there is a lot to do, the future looks promising. Thank you for that.”

30.speaker: Player
30.text: “Words are just words. Actions are what's important.”

31.speaker: Nia Morgna
31.text: “And you seem to be doing well at both so far. Pros are cancelling out the cons for sure.”

32.speaker: Nia Morgna
32.text: “How are you really holding up, Anton? Being the President, I mean.”

34.speaker: Nia Morgna
34.text: “You are giving me hope that this country can get better.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “It's not a matter of it *can* or it *can't*. It *will* get better. We will make it so.”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “Your support gives me hope as well.”

37.speaker: Nia Morgna
37.text: “We are all in this together after all.”

38.speaker: Nia Morgna
38.text: “I will follow you anywhere, as long as you keep making good decisions for the country.”

39.speaker: Nia Morgna
39.text: “For now, I just want to chat.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: “It's the hardest thing I have ever done in my life but it is also the best thing I have ever done in my life.”

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “It feels like the whole weight of the country crushes me down every single day.”

43.speaker: Nia Morgna
43.text: “Very well. I will take your word on that.”

44.speaker: Nia Morgna
44.text: “I can imagine. So much responsibility and so much power at the same time.”

45.speaker: Nia Morgna
45.text: “Everyone wants to be a president until they are one I guess.”

46.speaker: Nia Morgna
46.text: “I want to assist you and the country as best as I can. And to do that I have an idea. We need to eliminate the worst problem we have.”

48.speaker: Player
48.text: “Nonsense. Our government is not a corrupt government.”

50.speaker: Player
50.text: “So finally you come to the point. What do you really want?”

51.speaker: Nia Morgna
51.text: “Our government may not be, but think about the Supreme Court. Every single one of those Old Guards needs to answer to the law.”

52.speaker: Nia Morgna
52.text: “And it's not just the Old Guards. Think about the oligarchs. Everyone knows they have connections in the government. Who knows how deep the rabbit hole goes?”

53.speaker: Nia Morgna
53.text: “Please. Can't I hold a normal conversation with my president?”

54.speaker: Nia Morgna
54.text: “As the Minister of Justice, as you can guess, I have a passion for justice.”

55.speaker: Nia Morgna
55.text: “It's high time Old Guards and the Supreme Court stop holding the country in the palm of their hands.”

56.speaker: Nia Morgna
56.text: “That's why I want to form a new unit. The Anti-Corruption Police. That is my idea.”

57.speaker: Player
57.text: “Give me time to think about it.”

59.speaker: Player
59.text: “So? What if the anti-corruption police gets corrupted? What then?”

60.speaker: Nia Morgna
60.text: “I'm still figuring out the details myself right now, but of course there would be safety mechanisms in place.”

61.speaker: Nia Morgna
61.text: “I'm still figuring out the details myself right now, but think about the possibilities.”

62.speaker: Nia Morgna
62.text: “I'm glad you agree. I'm still figuring out the details myself right now, but think about the possibilities.”

66.speaker: Nia Morgna
66.text: “I want to assist you and the country as best as I can. Unfortunately, my hands are tied with the current budget allocation we have for the law enforceme--”

69.speaker: Nia Morgna
69.text: “I wouldn't trust her if I were--”

70.speaker: Lileas Graf
70.text: “I hope that I'm not interrupting your conversation.”

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: She barely finished the sentence before we heard a knock on the door. Nia almost jumped in her chair. Lileas Graf entered the room.

76.speaker: Nia Morgna
76.text: “A chat about the so called *reform* package.”

80.speaker: Nia Morgna
80.text: “No need to go on defensive. But I will say this.”

81.speaker: Nia Morgna
81.text: “Nothing. Apart from the fact that we are repeating Soll's mistakes again.”

82.speaker: Nia Morgna
82.text: “Or the fact that this is not what we were elected for.”

83.speaker: Nia Morgna
83.text: “Or the fact that...You get my point.”

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “Times change. Internal and external threats have to be eliminated.”

88.speaker: Nia Morgna
88.text: “This is not what we were elected for.”

89.speaker: Player
89.text: “Soll's mistakes? He made this great country what it currently is.”

90.speaker: Nia Morgna
90.text: “A place where there are innocent people getting murdered on the streets because of internal conflicts. Is this your understanding of a great country?”

91.speaker: Nia Morgna
91.text: “Times do change but the methods clearly not.”

93.speaker: Nia Morgna
93.text: “I keep thinking about it and I come to the same conclusion every time. There is no way I can get behind this. Don't forget that I have a vote in the Court.”

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “Trust me. I am doing all of this for the well being of Sordland.”

95.speaker: Player
95.text: “Enough. I already made my decision and what is left is for you to follow it.”

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: She opened her mouth to answer but there was knock at the door. Lileas Graf entered the room.

98.speaker: Nia Morgna
98.text: “No, not at all. We were just discussing...a few things.”

102.speaker: Lileas Graf
102.text: “We will provide a brief update on the situation of law enforcement.”

103.speaker: Nia Morgna
103.text: “The Ministry of Justice and the Supreme Court is working in close collaboration with the Ministry of Interior to address the protests in the country.”

104.speaker: Nia Morgna
104.text: “I must add that thanks to the hard work of our judiciary, the law enforcement forces assigned to my ministry are doing their jobs efficiently.”

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: Lileas took the seat next to Nia as she continued talking.

111.speaker: Nia Morgna
111.text: “Our efforts ramped up quite a bit recently. Especially after the declaration of the emergency decree.”

112.speaker: Lileas Graf
112.text: “I would call it the success of our forces on the ground, not due to the judicial branch of our government.”

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: Lileas shot Nia a brief withering glance.

120.speaker: Lileas Graf
120.text: “As expected, after the budget reduction, the morale of the employees are at an all time low. Many of them face the risk of losing their jobs now.”

121.speaker: Nia Morgna
121.text: “Agreed. The Ministry of Justice was hit the worst. The backlog of the court cases are so high that the judges do not even have time to look at smaller cases, postponing these to months or years later.”

125.speaker: Lileas Graf
125.text: “This comes at an even bigger surprise considering one of the promises that you have made was to focus on our security forces. Yet here we are, thinking about how to fire our security force personnel during mass protests.”

127.speaker: Lileas Graf
127.text: “Yet here we are, with mass protests happening in the country, talking about how we have to fire our security force personnel.”

128.speaker: Nia Morgna
128.text: “This causes a disastrous bottleneck. How can we deal justice if we can't even find time for these cases?”

129.speaker: Lileas Graf
129.text: “As expected, the budget increase has boosted morale of the employees in the law enforcement agencies. In these dire times, my people and Nia's people are especially delighted.”

130.speaker: Nia Morgna
130.text: “Agreed. At the Ministry of Justice, we are very happy with the decision as well. The backlog of the court cases are dwindling and we have started to fulfil the needs of the current situation.”

134.speaker: Lileas Graf
134.text: “And for that, all I will say is... Bravo! This was an excellent decision.”

135.speaker: Lileas Graf
135.text: “I think you will be glad to hear that the support for you among the forces is at an all time high, Mr. President.”

136.speaker: Lileas Graf
136.text: “This came as a pleasant surprise to many in the Ministry of the Interior since it was not even one of our campaign promises.”

137.speaker: Nia Morgna
137.text: “Certainly a step in the right direction.”

138.speaker: Lileas Graf
138.text: “The current budget has dampened hopes of more funding in the force.”

139.speaker: Nia Morgna
139.text: “Agreed. Many in the Ministry of Justice hoped for an increase and were not satisfied with the decision.”

143.speaker: Lileas Graf
143.text: “The decisions made needs to reflect the current situation of the country. This was certainly not the right decision when we are dealing with mass protests.”

144.speaker: Lileas Graf
144.text: “This comes at an even bigger surprise considering one of the promises that you have made was to focus on our security forces. Yet here we are, exactly where we started at.”

145.speaker: Lileas Graf
145.text: “Yet here we are, with mass protests happening in the country. We are standing exactly where we were before.”

146.speaker: Nia Morgna
146.text: “Regardless, this means we will have to deal with the growing court backlog. It is manageable but it will be a challenge for sure.”

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “Thank you. I am glad you approve.”

148.speaker: Player
148.text: “I did what was expected from me. That's all.”

149.speaker: Player
149.text: “Of course it was the right decision. I made it after all.”

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: Nia cast a sidelong look at Lileas.

155.speaker: Player
155.text: “Don't worry. I am sure you will manage.”

156.speaker: Player
156.text: “I had to make sacrifices for the good of Sordland.”

157.speaker: Player
157.text: “You will do as you are told with what you have.”

158.speaker: Lileas Graf
158.text: “These sacrifices might've very well damaged the structural integrity of Sordland.”

159.speaker: Nia Morgna
159.text: “That remains to be seen but the ripples are already being felt across the country. I hope this decision is not the beginning of something bad.”

160.speaker: Lileas Graf

161.speaker: Nia Morgna

171.speaker: Lileas Graf
171.text: “Well then. Let's move on to what we are actually here for.”

172.speaker: Lileas Graf
172.text: “Due to the budget increase, we can start doing much more as the main branches of security in Sordland.”

177.speaker: Player
177.text: “Why should I pick Ministry of Interior?”

178.speaker: Player
178.text: “Why should I pick Ministry of Justice?”

179.speaker: Lileas Graf
179.text: “The Ministry of Interior is a much more significant and important government agency that is in need of the funds. Especially during these times where there are many protests in the country.”

180.speaker: Lileas Graf
180.text: “This seems to be an organizational issue, not a funding one. The Interior needs the money more for the police and local governments.”

181.speaker: Player
181.text: “What if I decide to balance the budget in between Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice?”

182.speaker: Lileas Graf
182.text: “Balancing the budget won't help as much. The current situation clearly demands that a decisive choice be made to benefit the nation. ”

183.speaker: Lileas Graf
183.text: “Exactly. When deciding you must look at the bigger picture. I believe you will make the right choice and pick the Ministry of Interior.”

184.speaker: Nia Morgna
184.text: “I agree. We need to focus on one ministry to achieve tangible results.”

185.speaker: Nia Morgna
185.text: “A decision has to be made about the budget balance between the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Justice.”

186.speaker: Nia Morgna
186.text: “Good luck prosecuting criminals or going through local government laws without enough judges, Lileas.”

187.speaker: Nia Morgna
187.text: “Each day the stacks of legal cases are piling up for judges. Cases for corruption and criminals are delayed due to a lack of funds.

188.speaker: Nia Morgna
188.text: “Of course what would make the most sense in the current situation would be to support the much neglected Ministry of Justice that would improve the legal system in Sordland.”

201.speaker: Lileas Graf

244.speaker: Player
244.text: “Budget will be cut equally from the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice.”

245.speaker: Lileas Graf
245.text: “Ministry of Interior and our police forces on the ground play a much larger and a more important role during these times where there is a threat to our internal safety.”

246.speaker: Lileas Graf
246.text: “Simple. It's because Ministry of Interior can't afford a reduction unless you want the whole country to be overrun with protestors.”

247.speaker: Nia Morgna
247.text: “The Ministry of Interior is one of the well funded government agencies in Sordland. The same can't be said about Ministry of Justice.”

248.speaker: Nia Morgna
248.text: “We need decisive action. Cutting funding from both branches won't help anyone.”

249.speaker: Nia Morgna
249.text: “Hah. And tell me Lileas, how are you going to bring the criminals to justice if our judges have to postpone court dates to 6 months, 1 year later.”

250.speaker: Lileas Graf
250.text: “That doesn't mean anything. The Ministry of Interior is far more critical in function. Especially now.”

251.speaker: Lileas Graf
251.text: “Tell me, Nia. Who brings the criminals before the justices? Let me answer. The police forces connected to Ministry of Interior.”

252.speaker: Nia Morgna
252.text: “Look at it this way. Ministry of Justice has never been well-funded in Sordland while the Ministry of Interior was always more lucky, already causing this uneven balance in between the two.”

253.speaker: Nia Morgna
253.text: “Our court cases have been piling up with no end in sight. We already have a bottleneck. If we worsen the situation, our whole justice system will fall.”

254.speaker: Nia Morgna
254.text: “It doesn't even matter who or how many criminals you catch with your forces if justice can't be dealt.”

261.speaker: Lileas Graf
261.text: “This is completely absurd and unbefitting for the President of Sordland.”

263.speaker: Nia Morgna
263.text: “I knew you would see reason. Thank you.”

266.speaker: Lileas Graf
266.text: “I knew that we would be on the same side, Mr. President.”

273.speaker: Nia Morgna
273.text: “The right choice. It was time that Ministry of Justice got the funds it needs.”

275.speaker: Nia Morgna
275.text: “I was expecting you to be different, Mr. President.”

281.speaker: Lileas Graf
281.text: “Before you decide, I would like to remind you of your obligations and promises as the leader of this administration, Mr. President.”

298.speaker: Nia Morgna
298.text: “I must return to the ministry to implement necessary changes.”

325.text: “That's why I am proposing the formation of a Secret State Police.”

327.speaker: Lileas Graf
327.text: “We have been battling with terror for a long time now. I want to put an end to it.”

333.speaker: Lileas Graf
333.text: “You are making one good decision after another today, Mr. President.”

335.speaker: Lileas Graf

381.speaker: Nia Morgna
381.text: “As a sub branch of Ministry of Justice, the ACP would be given full authority by the Presidency to investigate corrupt government officials and citizens.”

382.speaker: Nia Morgna
382.text: “The Community Police would be picked from trustworthy members of the local community. It will give us greater coverage over the country to combat criminals.”

480.speaker: Lileas Graf
480.text: “I am sorry for being late. There was an important matter at the ministry. The security forces of Bergia are arbitrarily not cooperating with my department and created some minor annoyances.”

481.speaker: Lileas Graf
481.text: “Luckily they didn't completely botch their tasks, and actually uncovered a large network of priests that are recruiting Bergians for the Bludish Freedom Front.”

482.speaker: Player
482.text: "This sounds very significant. Do you want to explain more?"

483.speaker: Player
483.text: "Good. Do your best to keep the miscommunication with the Governor's forces to a minimum. We need to take the war against terror seriously."

484.speaker: Player
484.text: "You were late, Ms. Graf. But now that you are here, let's begin with the meeting."

486.speaker: Lileas Graf
486.text: "The issue was a miscommunication about an ongoing investigation inside Bergia. But as I said, it didn't affect the results in a negative way."

487.speaker: Lileas Graf
487.text: "The investigation itself, however, revealed some troubling facts. We suspect the existence of a massive network of BFF-aligned priests currently serving in Bergia."

488.speaker: Lileas Graf
488.text: "We have discovered that most of the existing Golcondist sanctuaries and communities inside Bergia are indeed working directly for the BFF."

489.speaker: Lileas Graf
489.text: "Several reports also point to a possible infiltration of the Dastnurist and Wruhecist communities by these Golcondist sects. May the Divine God forgive us if this is true."

490.speaker: Player
490.text: "Thank you for the brief report, Lileas."

491.speaker: Player
491.text: "This is worrying news. Keep following the lead. We cannot let these sects divide our society."

493.speaker: Lileas Graf
493.text: "If you want my honest opinion, they are a group of dangerous radicals who follow a warped interpretation of Wruhecist Nurity. Most faithful Nurists wouldn't want to have anything to do with them."

494.speaker: Nia Morgna
494.text: "I don't appreciate you speaking like that, Lileas. The majority of the Bludish community in Sordland practice Golcondism."

495.speaker: Lileas Graf
495.text: "Don't normalize it, Ms. Morgna. They are a plague on this earth. Even orthodox Wruhecists do not like them."

496.speaker: Lileas Graf
496.text: "As a devout Dastnurist myself, I haven't experienced any divide in Sordland between our religion and mainstream Wruhecism. Bless St. Dast -- all practitioners of Nurity live in peace here..."

497.speaker: Lileas Graf
497.text: "...Except the Golcondists, of course. Their extremist beliefs are an abomination. And unfortunately, after the Wruhecist Revolution in Derdia, now we also have a Golcondist state that uses the influence of their faith internationally."

498.speaker: Lileas Graf
498.text: "As a matter of fact, the Nurist Republic of Derdia is one of the BFF's suspected supporters. Their aims are clearly one and the same."

501.speaker: Player
501.text: "Do you suspect any other countries are supporting the BFF together with Derdia?"

502.speaker: Player
502.text: "Keep following that lead. We cannot let countries like Derdia try and destabilize us with religion."

504.speaker: Lileas Graf
504.text: "I suspect the Kingdom of Rizia is involved in this along with Derdia. However, the biggest player is Rumburg and we have clear evidence of their interference. Our focus must be on them."

505.speaker: Nia Morgna
505.text: "I don't think we should damage our international relations over unproven suspicions. Our direct neighbors have much more influence over us."

506.speaker: Nia Morgna
506.text: "Besides, this isn't the topic of this meeting. I think it's best to discuss this in an external security meeting -- when or if -- enough proof is collected."

511.speaker: Lileas Graf
511.text: "I thought you'd be familiar with them as a Bergian yourself."

512.speaker: Lileas Graf
512.text: "I thought you might have encountered them during your university days."

516.speaker: Player
516.text: "To be honest, I couldn't care less about religion."

517.speaker: Lileas Graf
517.text: "May the Divine God save your soul."

518.speaker: Nia Morgna
518.text: "If this is over, why don't we start the meeting?"

519.speaker: Lileas Graf
519.text: "Unfortunately, due to my limited authority in the Special Zone of Bergia, I cannot control their operations."
